title: Pinning Decisions Before Failure: Executable Records of Underspecified Choices in AI-Assisted Code Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.03237v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A natural-language requirement leaves questions open, and a model asked to implement it settles them silently: across 600 generated test suites from three models, 42.7% contain no test that distinguishes the competing readings. An acceptance example written before implementing is the usual remedy, but an example both readings satisfy resolves nothing.   We insert two steps into that practice: enumerate the requirement's underspecified points by name, then for each construct two throwaway implementations differing only in that point and keep a candidate input only if executing both shows they disagree. The result is recorded as a decision pin: the named point, the confirmed input, and the value the person chose between the two exhibited results. translated_title: 在失败之前固定决策：AI辅助代码生成中欠明确选择的可执行记录
translated_abstract: 自然语言需求会留下悬而未决的问题，而被要求实现该需求的模型会悄然自行做出决定：在来自三个模型的600个生成测试套件中，42.7%不包含任何能够区分相互竞争的不同解读的测试。在实现之前编写验收示例是常用的补救办法，但两种解读都能满足的示例解决不了任何问题。我们在这一实践中插入两个步骤：首先按名称逐一列举需求中欠明确的要点，然后针对每个要点构造两个仅在该要点上有所不同的临时实现，只有当执行两者显示出结果分歧时才保留候选输入。其结果被记录为一个“决策钉”（decision pin）：包含被命名的要点、经过确认的输入，以及人在两个展示出的结果之间所选择的值。同一条记录随后既约束代码生成过程，也通过执行来判定合规性。在一个包含40个任务、配有成对参考实现的基准测试上，针对两个模型，区分性输入的获取率……（摘要截断）
tldr: 提出“决策钉”方法：通过显式列举需求中的欠明确要点、构造仅在该要点上不同的两个临时实现并用执行验证得到可区分二者的输入，将人对歧义点的选择固化为可执行记录，从而约束AI代码生成并通过执行判定合规性。
en_tdlr: Proposes "decision pins"—executable records of underspecified choices that enumerate named ambiguity points in requirements, construct throwaway implementation pairs differing only in one point to find execution-confirmed separating inputs, and record the human's chosen value to constrain AI code generation and decide compliance by execution.
